Maintenance Report — MNT-0002-006

Asset: WELL-0002 (SW-23 Well 002, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: rod string Work started: 09 Nov 2024 08:00 · Finished: 13 Nov 2024 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 102 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0002-0040 on 2024-11-07 Report written: 14 Nov 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0002-0040 showed the wellhead at 19.5 °C with the air at 13.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Rod couplings1,141
Fishing tool rental1,901

Total11,816

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0002-009

Asset: WELL-0002 (SW-23 Well 002, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 15 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 02 Sep 2025 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 428 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0002-0080 on 2025-08-14 Report written: 04 Sep 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0002-0080 showed the wellhead at 35.7 °C with the air at 34.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 239 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 191 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0002-009 (WS-06).

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0002-013

Asset: WELL-0002 (SW-23 Well 002, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 06 Feb 2026 08:00 · Finished: 06 Feb 2026 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0002-0105 on 2026-02-05 Report written: 06 Feb 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0002-0105 at 08:00 on 2026-02-05 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.6% of the pad area, estimated 5.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 239 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 191 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 4.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0002-013 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.5% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
